evidence.actual: absent: the Response has no ds:Signature child
evidence.expected: A signature on the Response or on the inner Assertion, verifiable against the configured IdP certificate

evidence.actual: Contains Issuer, Status (Success) and an EncryptedAssertion holding only an xenc:EncryptedData block (aes256-cbc, cipher value redacted). No Signature is visible anywhere.
evidence.note: The assertion is opaque until it is decrypted. Any signature inside it can't be checked from this capture. Destination, InResponseTo, Issuer and Status all match the expected values.

output.fix: Configure the IdP to sign the Response, or to sign the Assertion before encrypting it. Preferably sign both. On the SP, require a signature that verifies against the configured IdP certificate (not a key embedded in the message), and reject any response where neither element is signed. If you can, verify the Response signature before decrypting anything. After decryption, re-check the Audience, Conditions, Recipient, NameID format and required attributes (email, firstName) on the inner assertion.

alternatives.why_not: Nothing in the capture shows a decryption failure. The cause would only change if the SP's decrypt log reports one.
The Response is unsigned and the assertion can't be inspected, so it can't be said to validate.
